conceptZh: 狼是會對著月亮嚎叫的野獸
object: a caped action-figure hero with an absurdly long cape and a bouncing moon-shaped ball
morph: a rubber ball ricochets around the frame and each hit drops one stroke of 狼 into place
creativeAngle: 披風太長的英雄被球砸中，每次彈跳掉下一筆；詞用「大野狼」，披風遮住頭變成狼耳。
promptEn: An 8-second animated clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 狼 (wolf). Lead: a stiff toy hero with a bright teal cape three sizes too long that drags and flops over his face. Moment 1 (0-1.7s): he strikes a heroic pose on a hill, tangles in the cape, and a pale round ball bounces in; the voice says 狼 as it bonks his helmet. Moment 2 (1.7-3.4s): the ball ricochets off a tree, a rock, the cape; each hit knocks a blue stroke from the sky into place, the second 狼 landing on the final stroke so the glyph stands complete. Moment 3 (3.4-5.2s): the cape flips over his head, the two pointed corners poking up like ears; peeking out with a growl-shaped grin he pretends to howl silently at the ball moon as the voice says 大野狼, a fuzzy gray cartoon wolf cub popping up beside him copying the pose. Moment 4 (5.2-8s): glyph still; hero and cub howl-pose together, cape flapping. Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "狼、狼、大野狼" (ㄌㄤˊ、ㄌㄤˊ、ㄉㄚˋ ㄧㄝˇ ㄌㄤˊ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, then stops; no other speech, no music louder than the voice. The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 狼, drawn as saturated solid midnight-blue strokes on a soft yellow background, correctly formed, centered, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold while the lead keeps a small joyful motion away from the strokes. No vocabulary text, subtitles, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.

conceptZh: 玩具戰士坐上投石器想衝向大野狼布偶，浣熊花生敬禮時手肘誤觸把手提早發射，戰士轉著圈飛過狼的頭頂、砰地撞上籬笆柱再倒栽進水桶，花生那疊紅色泡棉條被震落，一根根掉在中間排成「狼」字。
object: a chunky plastic toy warrior with a foam sword and round shield loaded in a toy catapult, aiming at a big fluffy grey cartoon wolf plush; Peanut the raccoon beside the lever with a wobbling stack of deep-red foam bars
morph: the warrior is launched too early, spins past the wolf, BONKs off a fence post and drops upside-down into a bucket; the impact shakes Peanut's stack loose and the red foam bars tumble into the empty center, settling as the strokes of 狼 (犭 on the left, 良 on the right)
creativeAngle: 上一版是披風英雄與彈跳球，這版換成全新的「發射」橋段：戰士被提早彈射、飛過目標、撞柱反彈倒栽進水桶，四個段落各有新動作，筆畫直接由撞擊震落的泡棉條堆成，而「大野狼」一詞由畫面上的狼布偶起身做嚎叫姿勢來呼應，聽到什麼就看到什麼。
promptEn:
An 8-second animated slapstick clip teaching the Traditional Chinese character 狼 (wolf). Setting: a flat sunny backyard stage on a soft pale-mint background, nothing busy behind. Lead: a chunky plastic toy warrior with a foam sword, a round shield and a big brave chin, all bravado and no skill. Buddy: Peanut, a cartoon raccoon hugging a wobbling stack of deep-red foam bars far taller than himself.

Moment 1 (0-1.7s): on the left the warrior sits loaded in the cup of a wooden toy catapult and points his foam sword across the frame at a big fluffy grey cartoon wolf plush sitting on the right, grinning harmlessly. The off-screen voice says 狼 the first time exactly as he points at the wolf. Peanut waddles up beside the catapult lever, stack swaying.

Moment 2 (1.7-3.4s): the warrior strikes a drumroll pose, knees bouncing, counting down with the sword. Peanut salutes at exactly the wrong moment, his elbow bumps the lever, and WHOOSH the warrior is flung early in a huge arc across the top of the frame. He swings his sword so hard mid-air that he spins like a pinwheel and sails right over the wolf's head while the wolf calmly watches him go by.

Moment 3 (3.4-5.2s): BONK, he squashes flat against a tall wooden fence post at the far right with cartoon squash-and-stretch, wobbles, and rebounds backward to drop upside-down into a tin bucket, boots kicking in the air. The impact jolts Peanut's whole stack loose: the red foam bars tumble into the empty center of the frame and settle one by one into the strokes of 狼, the three strokes of 犭 on the left, then 良 on the right. The voice says 狼 the second time exactly as the last stroke clicks into place.

Moment 4 (5.2-8s): the finished glyph stands perfectly still and readable in the center. The voice says 大野狼 and the big fluffy wolf plush in the lower right pops upright, tips its head back in a proud silent howl pose and waves a paw. In the lower left the warrior wriggles out of the bucket with a dizzy grin, raises his foam sword in a tiny wobbly victory pose, and Peanut salutes him, late again. Nobody touches or covers the strokes.

Audio: a warm, friendly off-screen voice in clear Taiwanese Mandarin reads exactly "狼、狼、大野狼" (ㄌㄤˊ、ㄌㄤˊ、ㄉㄚˋ ㄧㄝˇ ㄌㄤˊ), slowly and distinctly with clear tones, with a short pause between each utterance, then stops. No other speech, no subtitles, no music louder than the voice; soft cartoon boing and bonk sounds only.

The only on-screen text is the single Traditional Chinese glyph 狼, drawn as saturated solid deep-red strokes on the pale-mint background, correctly formed, centered, uncropped, filling about 70% of frame height with margins, perfectly still for the final 3-second hold. No vocabulary text, watermark, clutter, flashing, real people or realistic humans; bright but not neon, no dark grading.
